name: Priya Halvorsen-Nwosu
description: Priya Halvorsen-Nwosu rose from a Tier 2 transit-worker family in the Lakeshore Corridor to become GLMZ's most-subscribed emotional-broadcast personality, known professionally as 'Rawfeed Priya.' Her feeds are unfiltered BCI streams — she broadcasts grief, joy, and physical sensation without editorial compression, which corporate feed-curators call 'unsafe bandwidth.' She famously streamed the entire 36-hour experience of giving birth to her daughter Sable in 2218, which drew 4.2 million simultaneous neural connections and crashed two relay nodes.
cultural_impact: Priya's uncompressed feed style spawned the 'Rawcast' movement, where thousands of amateur broadcasters reject emotion-smoothing filters as corporate sanitization. Her popularity has forced three major BCI platform providers to offer unfiltered subscription tiers, reshaping how emotional data is monetized.
locations: Node 7 Relay Station (where her birth-stream crashed the grid)
story_hooks: Priya's daughter Sable was born with a rare BCI sensitivity that makes her passively receive nearby emotional broadcasts — someone is exploiting this, feeding Sable curated trauma to shape her emotional baseline for a future corporate contract.
A competing feed-star has begun mirroring Priya's exact emotional signature in their broadcasts, too precisely to be coincidence — someone has stolen or synthesized her neural pattern.
Priya receives an anonymous feed-packet containing 11 minutes of her own memories she has no recollection of — memories set in a Tier 5 Spire facility she has never visited.
controversy: In 2220 she broadcast a feed during a CorpSec raid on her building, capturing officer identification data in her emotional stream; two officers were later prosecuted using her feed as evidence, and CorpSec has never forgiven her.
